title: Math · Grade 4
description: An original starter path: build the idea, work an example, then try it. A focused introduction, ready to grow with your class.
framework: Original introductory mathematics practice; suggested grade placement, not a complete standards syllabus.
sequenceNote: Suggested teaching sequence, not mandated unit order.
alignmentNote: Starter course; not full grade-level coverage.

lessons.title: Scale a fraction
lessons.reading: Multiply numerator and denominator by the same nonzero number to make an equivalent fraction. Both the parts and selected parts are subdivided equally.
lessons.easyReading: Multiply numerator and denominator by the same nonzero number to make an equivalent fraction. Both the parts and selected parts are subdivided equally.
lessons.expertReading: Multiply numerator and denominator by the same nonzero number to make an equivalent fraction. Both the parts and selected parts are subdivided equally. Multiplying by a fraction equal to one preserves value.
lessons.worked: 2/3 = 4/6 because each third is split into two sixths.
steps: 2/3 = 4/6 because each third is split into two sixths.

application.explanation: 6/8. Multiply numerator and denominator by the same nonzero number to make an equivalent fraction. Both the parts and selected parts are subdivided equally.

vocab.definition: Fractions that name the same number.

lessons.practice: Explain how equivalent fractions helps solve the question. Include the numbers or properties that support your answer.
lessons.reflection: 6/8. Multiply numerator and denominator by the same nonzero number to make an equivalent fraction. Both the parts and selected parts are subdivided equally.

lessons.title: Add equal-sized parts
lessons.reading: Add fractions with a common denominator by counting their numerators together. The size of each part stays the same.
lessons.easyReading: Add fractions with a common denominator by counting their numerators together. The size of each part stays the same.
lessons.expertReading: Add fractions with a common denominator by counting their numerators together. The size of each part stays the same. A denominator acts like a unit label when adding fractions.
lessons.worked: 2/7 + 3/7 = 5/7 because two sevenths plus three sevenths make five sevenths.
steps: 2/7 + 3/7 = 5/7 because two sevenths plus three sevenths make five sevenths.

application.explanation: 5/8. Add fractions with a common denominator by counting their numerators together. The size of each part stays the same.

vocab.definition: The number of equal parts counted by a fraction.

lessons.practice: Explain how numerator helps solve the question. Include the numbers or properties that support your answer.
lessons.reflection: 5/8. Add fractions with a common denominator by counting their numerators together. The size of each part stays the same.

lessons.title: Multiply by a whole number
lessons.reading: Multiplying a fraction by a whole number repeats that fraction. Multiply its numerator while keeping the part size.
lessons.easyReading: Multiplying a fraction by a whole number repeats that fraction. Multiply its numerator while keeping the part size.
lessons.expertReading: Multiplying a fraction by a whole number repeats that fraction. Multiply its numerator while keeping the part size. Improper fractions can represent quantities greater than or equal to one.
lessons.worked: 3 × 2/5 = 6/5 because three groups of two fifths contain six fifths.
steps: 3 × 2/5 = 6/5 because three groups of two fifths contain six fifths.

application.explanation: 4/3. Multiplying a fraction by a whole number repeats that fraction. Multiply its numerator while keeping the part size.

vocab.definition: A fraction whose numerator is at least its positive denominator.

lessons.practice: Explain how improper fraction helps solve the question. Include the numbers or properties that support your answer.
lessons.reflection: 4/3. Multiplying a fraction by a whole number repeats that fraction. Multiply its numerator while keeping the part size.

lessons.title: Tenths and hundredths
lessons.reading: Decimals extend place value to parts smaller than one. Ten hundredths equal one tenth, just as ten ones equal one ten.
lessons.easyReading: Decimals extend place value to parts smaller than one. Ten hundredths equal one tenth, just as ten ones equal one ten.
lessons.expertReading: Decimals extend place value to parts smaller than one. Ten hundredths equal one tenth, just as ten ones equal one ten. Trailing zeros after the decimal can change the displayed precision without changing numerical value.
lessons.worked: 0.4 = 0.40 because four tenths equal forty hundredths.
steps: 0.4 = 0.40 because four tenths equal forty hundredths.

application.explanation: 0.70. Decimals extend place value to parts smaller than one. Ten hundredths equal one tenth, just as ten ones equal one ten.

vocab.definition: A number written using base-ten places, including places smaller than one.

lessons.practice: Explain how decimal helps solve the question. Include the numbers or properties that support your answer.
lessons.reflection: 0.70. Decimals extend place value to parts smaller than one. Ten hundredths equal one tenth, just as ten ones equal one ten.

lessons.title: Measure a turn
lessons.reading: An angle measures the turn between two rays sharing an endpoint. A right angle measures 90 degrees.
lessons.easyReading: An angle measures the turn between two rays sharing an endpoint. A right angle measures 90 degrees.
lessons.expertReading: An angle measures the turn between two rays sharing an endpoint. A right angle measures 90 degrees. Adjacent angle measures add when their interiors do not overlap.
lessons.worked: Half of a straight 180° turn is a right 90° turn.
steps: Half of a straight 180° turn is a right 90° turn.

application.prompt: An angle measures 35°. How much more makes 90°?
application.explanation: 55°. An angle measures the turn between two rays sharing an endpoint. A right angle measures 90 degrees.

vocab.definition: A figure formed by two rays sharing an endpoint.

lessons.practice: Explain how angle helps solve the question. Include the numbers or properties that support your answer.
lessons.reflection: 55°. An angle measures the turn between two rays sharing an endpoint. A right angle measures 90 degrees.
